record.title: Equality of past-information and ordinary detection thresholds
record.statement:
Let $d$ be the spatial dimension. Let $\lambda_\mathrm{c}$ be the critical intensity for the relevant space-time percolation transition, and let $\lambda_\mathrm{past}$ be the smallest value such that, when $\lambda>\lambda_\mathrm{past}$, a target that cannot foresee future node locations is eventually detected almost surely. **Past-information threshold conjecture.** For all dimensions $d\geq 1$, we have

$$
\lambda_\mathrm{past}=\lambda_\mathrm{c}.
$$

The conjecture concerns targets whose position at time $s$ may depend only on node positions during $[0,s)$. The source gives no resolution, so the equality remains open; the stated inequalities place this threshold between $\lambda_\mathrm{c}$ and $\lambda_\mathrm{t}$.
record.source_name: Alexandre Stauffer, “Space-time percolation and detection by mobile nodes”, arXiv:1108.6322 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1108.6322

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2011).

record.title: Conjecture on 0123-avoiding ascent sequences and bounded-height Dyck paths
record.statement: Let $A_{0123}(n)$ be the number of ascent sequences of length $n$ avoiding $0123$. A Dyck path of semilength $n$ has height at most $5$ if its maximum vertical height is at most $5$. **The 0123 Dyck-path conjecture.** $A_{0123}(n)$ equals the number of Dyck paths of semilength $n$ and height at most $5$. The conjecture identifies the enumeration of 0123-avoiding ascent sequences with a bounded-height Dyck-path family; the source gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Paul Duncan and Einar Steingrimsson, “Pattern avoidance in ascent sequences”, arXiv:1109.3641 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1109.3641

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2011).

record.title: Bollobás and Scott's logarithmic heavy cycle conjecture
record.statement:
Let $D$ be a **weighted loopless digraph** with $n\geq 2$ vertices. For each vertex $v\in V(D)$, write $d^{w+}(v)$ for its weighted outdegree, and write $w(C)$ for the total weight of a directed cycle $C$. **Bollobás and Scott's conjecture.** If

$$
d^{w+}(v)\geq 1
$$

for every vertex $v\in V(D)$, then $D$ contains a directed cycle $C$ such that

$$
w(C)\geq \frac{2}{\log_2 n}.
$$

The conjecture strengthens the known lower bound $(24n)^{-1/3}$ and is motivated by constructions whose maximum cycle weight is at most a constant multiple of $\log_2\log_2 n/\log_2 n$. Its status is not resolved in the supplied source material.
record.source_name: Binlong Li and Shenggui Zhang, “A note on heavy cycles in weighted digraphs”, arXiv:1109.4676 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1109.4676

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of September 2011). “This conjecture was disproved by T. Spencer of Nebraska {(See )}.”

record.title: Derived generalized Auslander–Reiten conjecture
record.statement:
Let $R$ be a left Noetherian ring, let ${\sf D}^b(R)$ be the bounded derived category of finitely generated left $R$-modules, and write $X\perp Y$ when $\operatorname{Hom}_{{\sf D}^b(R)}(X,\Sigma^iY)=0$ for all integers $i\gg 0$. Let ${\sf Thick}(R)$ denote the smallest thick subcategory of ${\sf D}^b(R)$ containing $R$. **Derived generalized Auslander–Reiten conjecture.** If $M\in{\sf D}^b(R)$ satisfies

$$
M\perp M\qquad\text{and}\qquad M\perp R,
$$

then $M$ belongs to ${\sf Thick}(R)$. This is the derived-category version proposed in the paper; the authors explain that it is equivalent to the classical generalized conjecture for modules and is preserved under derived equivalence.
record.source_name: Kosmas Diveris and Marju Purin, “A Generalization of the Auslander-Reiten Conjecture for the Bounded Derived Category”, arXiv:1109.6072 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1109.6072

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of September 2011).

record.title: Martin's maximum conjecture for forcing extensions of $H_{\aleph_2}$
record.statement:
Let $V$ be a model of ${\text{{\sf MM}}}^{++}$ together with large cardinals, and let $P\in V$ preserve ${\text{{\sf MM}}}^{++}$. **Martin's maximum conjecture.** For every such $P$,

$$
H_{\aleph_2}^V\prec H_{\aleph_2}^{V^P}.
$$

This conjecture concerns the invariance of the first-order theory of $H_{\aleph_2}$ under forcing that preserves ${\text{{\sf MM}}}^{++}$. The supplied text does not indicate whether it has been resolved.
record.source_name: Matteo Viale, “Martin's maximum revisited”, arXiv:1110.1181 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1110.1181

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2011).

record.title: Canonical-form conjecture for natural reorderings of finite connected quandles
record.statement:
Let $Q$ be a finite connected quandle with elements $1,2,\ldots,n$ naturally ordered, profile $\{1,\ell_1,\ell_2,\ldots,\ell_k\}$, and $1\leq\ell_1\leq\ell_2\leq\cdots\leq\ell_k$. Let $\nu$ be a natural reordering with respect to $r_n$, as in the last sentence of Theorem. **Canonical-form conjecture.** In the last sentence of Theorem, one can choose $\nu$ so that $\nu(i)=i$ for every integer $i$ satisfying

$$
\left(\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}\ell_j\right)+1\leq i\leq n
$$

even when $\ell_{k-1}=\ell_k$. This concerns whether the canonical-form construction can be strengthened when the two largest profile parts are equal. The supplied text gives no evidence that the assertion has been proved or disproved, so it remains open.
record.source_name: Chuichiro Hayashi, “Canonical forms for operation tables of finiate connected quandles”, arXiv:1110.1849 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1110.1849

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2011).

record.title: Concavity conjecture for maximal-area disk-polygons
record.statement:
Let $C$ be a circle of radius $r<1$, and let $P_n$ be an $n$-sided disk-polygon of largest area inscribed in $C$.

**Concavity conjecture for maximal-area disk-polygons.** For all $n\geq 4$,

$$
\operatorname{Area}(P_{n-1})+\operatorname{Area}(P_{n+1})<2\operatorname{Area}(P_n).
$$

The paper proves this inequality for odd $n$ with $n\geq 5$, but states that its method does not extend straightforwardly to all $n$ and that no general area formula is known. The conjecture extends the established odd-index case to every $n\geq4$.
record.source_name: Karoly Bezdek, Zsolt Langi, Marton Naszodi and Peter Papez, “Ball-Polyhedra”, arXiv:1110.4329 (2011).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1110.4329

record.title: The conjecture on the spectrum of growth rate functions for exponentially dense matroid classes
record.statement:
Let $q$ be a prime power, and let $\mathcal{M}$ be a **base-$q$ exponentially dense** minor-closed class of matroids, meaning that its growth rate is eventually of order $q^n$. Let $h_{\mathcal{M}}(n)$ denote the maximum size of a simple rank-$n$ matroid in $\mathcal{M}$. **Growth-rate spectrum conjecture.** There exist integers $k$ and $d$ with $k \ge 0$ and

$$
0 \le d \le \frac{q^{2k}-1}{q^2-1},
$$

such that

$$
h_{\mathcal{M}}(n)=\frac{q^{n+k}-1}{q-1}-qd
$$

for all sufficiently large $n$. This conjecture proposes that the displayed values are the extremes in a small spectrum of possible eventual growth rate functions; the source further conjectures that every allowable triple $(q,k,d)$ occurs for some minor-closed class.
record.source_name: Jim Geelen and Peter Nelson, “On minor-closed classes of matroids with exponential growth rate”, arXiv:1110.6668 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1110.6668

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2011).

record.title: The finite-range upper-bound conjecture for complete arcs in projective planes
record.statement:
Let $PG(2,q)$ be the projective plane of order $q$, and let $t_{2}(2,q)$ denote the smallest size of a complete arc in $PG(2,q)$. **The finite-range upper-bound conjecture.** In $PG(2,q)$,

$$
t_{2}(2,q)<5\sqrt{q}\quad \text{for }q\leq 8192.
$$

This conjecture gives a uniform numerical bound over the specified finite range of plane orders, extending the computational estimates discussed in the source. The supplied source gives no evidence that it has been resolved.
record.source_name: Daniele Bartoli, Alexander A. Davydov, Giorgio Faina, Stefano Marcugini and Fernanda Pambianco, “Upper bounds on the smallest size of a complete arc in the plane PG(2,q)”, arXiv:1111.3403 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1111.3403

record.title: The generic full-rank vertex-map conjecture for hom-polytopes
record.statement: Let $P(M)$ and $Q(M')$ be polytopes of dimensions $d$ and $e$, respectively, with $M\in R_{d,m}$ and $M'\in R'_{e,n}$, where $m\geq d+1$ and $n\geq e+1$. A vertex map $f:P(M)\to Q(M')$ has **full rank** when its rank is the maximum possible rank. **Generic full-rank vertex-map conjecture.** For any dimensions $d$ and $e$ and any integers $m\geq d+1$ and $n\geq e+1$, there is a dense open subset $U_{d,e,m,n}$ of $R_{d,m}\times R'_{e,n}$ such that if $(M,M')\in U_{d,e,m,n}$, then every vertex map $f:P(M)\to Q(M')$ of full rank is a simple vertex of $\operatorname{Hom}(P,Q)$. This would generalize the generic simplicity theorem for full-rank vertex maps to arbitrary dimensions.
record.source_name: Tristram Bogart, Mark Contois and Joseph Gubeladze, “Hom-polytopes”, arXiv:1111.3880 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1111.3880

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2011).

record.title: The small-parameter trace-Sperner asymptotic conjecture
record.statement:
Let $f(n,k,l)$ be the maximum size of an $l$-trace $k$-Sperner family ${\mathcal F}\subseteq 2^{[n]}$. For a family, being $l$-trace $k$-Sperner means that the trace on every $l$-set is $k$-Sperner. **Small-parameter trace-Sperner conjecture.** For every pair of integers $k\leq l'$, one has

$$
f(n,k,n-l')=\Theta_{k,l'}\left(\frac{1}{n^{l'-k+1}}\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}\right).
$$

The conjecture is proposed as a common generalization of the preceding results and conjectures for the case $k\leq l'$. The paper records partial estimates, including the cases $k=1$ and uniform families, but does not establish the asserted order of magnitude in general.
record.source_name: Balazs Patkos, “A note on traces of set families”, arXiv:1111.4636 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1111.4636

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2011).

record.title: Homology decomposition conjecture for skew lattices with one extremum
record.statement:
Let $L$ be a finite skew lattice, and let $L/\!\!\sim$ denote its quotient by the relevant equivalence relation. Assume that $L$ has either a unique minimum or a unique maximum. **Homology decomposition conjecture.** Then, for some nonnegative integers $p$ and $q$,

$$
H_n(L) \cong H_n(L/\!\!\sim)\oplus\operatorname{\mathbb{Z}}_{\gcd(a,b,c)}^p\oplus\operatorname{\mathbb{Z}}_{\gcd(a,b,c,d)}^q.
$$

The analogous decomposition is established when the skew lattice has both a unique minimum and a unique maximum, and computations verify the one-extremum version for all skew lattices with at most four elements. The general case remains open.
record.source_name: Jozef H. Przytycki and Krzysztof K. Putyra, “Homology of Distributive Lattices”, arXiv:1111.4772 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1111.4772

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2011).

record.title: Exact codegree threshold conjecture for $(K_4^3-e)$-factors
record.statement:
Let $t_2^3(n,K_4^3-e)$ be the smallest integer $d$ such that every 3-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices with minimum 2-degree at least $d$ contains a spanning collection of vertex-disjoint copies of $K_4^3-e$, where $K_4^3-e$ is the 3-graph on four vertices with three edges. **Exact threshold conjecture for $(K_4^3-e)$-factors.** For integers $n>8$ divisible by $4$,

$$
t_2^3(n,K_4^3-e)=n/2-1.
$$

The paper proves the lower bound $t_2^3(n,K_4^3-e)\ge n/2-1$ and an asymptotically matching upper bound, so the conjecture asserts the exact value for every admissible $n>8$. Its resolution is not specified in the supplied source.
record.source_name: Allan Lo and Klas Markström, “Minimum codegree threshold for (K_4^3-e)-factors”, arXiv:1111.5734 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1111.5734

record.title: Erdős's asymptotic conjecture on two complete 3-uniform subhypergraphs
record.statement: Let $s$ be a positive integer, and let $t(n,s,3)$ denote the maximum number of edges in a 3-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices containing no copy of $K_s^3$. **Erdős's conjecture.** There is an $n_0(s)$ such that every 3-uniform hypergraph on $n\geq n_0(s)$ vertices and $t(n,s,3)+1$ edges contains two $K_s^3$. This would give an affirmative answer to the first question for all sufficiently large $n$, whereas the examples in the paper show that the assertion fails for some small values of $n$.
record.source_name: Klas Markström, “Two questions of Erdős on hypergraphs above the Turán threshold”, arXiv:1111.5743 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1111.5743

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2011). “The conjecture remains open and the best current upper bound has been found by Razborov.”

record.title: Extremal hypergraph conjecture for bounded-degree spanning structures
record.statement:
Let $k\in\mathbb N$. A $k$-graph is a hypergraph whose edges have size $k$. Let $F$ be a forbidden hypergraph of bounded maximum vertex degree, and for each $v\in V$ let $F(v)$ denote the corresponding vertex-deleted hypergraph. **Extremal bounded-spanning-structure conjecture.** There exists $n_0$ such that, for every $k$-graph $H$ on $n\geq n_0$ vertices with no spanning subgraph isomorphic to $F$, one has

$$
|e(H)|\leq \binom{n-1}{k}+\operatorname{ex}\left(n-1,\{F(v):v\in V\}\right),
$$

and this bound is tight. The conjecture proposes that an extremal hypergraph for a bounded-degree spanning structure consists asymptotically of a complete $(n-1)$-vertex $k$-graph together with an extremal remainder. The supplied text gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Roman Glebov, Yury Person and Wilma Weps, “On extremal hypergraphs for hamiltonian cycles”, arXiv:1111.7028 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1111.7028

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2011).

record.title: Gao–Ruzsa–Thangadurai conjecture on Olson's constant in finite-dimensional vector spaces
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal OL(\mathbf F_p^d)$ denote the Olson constant of the additive group $\mathbf F_p^d$, namely the smallest integer such that no subset of that group of the given cardinality is zero-sum-free. **Gao–Ruzsa–Thangadurai conjecture.** For every fixed positive integer $d$ and all sufficiently large primes $p$,

$$
\mathcal OL(\mathbf F_p^d)=p+\mathcal OL(\mathbf F_p^{d-1})-1.
$$

The equality would determine Olson's constant recursively in fixed dimension. The source notes that the assumption that $p$ is sufficiently large is necessary, but gives no resolution of the conjecture.
record.source_name: Hoi H. Nguyen and Van Vu, “A characterization of incomplete sequences in F_p^d”, arXiv:1112.0754 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.0754

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2011).

record.title: The linearization maximum conjecture for set-system dimension
record.statement:
A **set system** is a family of sets, and its dimension $\dim \mathcal{X}$ is its learning-sequence order type. A **linearization** of a set system is a suitable set system preserving the relevant union structure and linearly ordered by inclusion. The paper asks whether

$$
\dim \mathcal{X}=\max\left\{\dim \mathcal{Y}\;;\;\mathcal{Y}\ \text{is a linearization of }\mathcal{X}\right\}
$$

for every set system $\mathcal{X}$. **Linearization maximum conjecture.** The displayed equality holds for every set system $\mathcal{X}$. This seeks a set-system analogue of the de Jongh–Parikh theorem for well-quasi-orders; the source formulates it as a question and does not provide a resolution.
record.source_name: Yohji Akama, “A new order theory of set systems and better quasi-orderings”, arXiv:1112.2801 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.2801

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2011).

record.title: Eventual periodicity for finite taking-no-breaking octal games under the disjunctive sum
record.statement:
Let $O=(n_1n_2\dots n_t,p_1p_2\dots p_t)$ and $P=(m_1m_2\dots m_l,q_1q_2\dots q_l)$ be two finite taking-no-breaking octal games. Assume that at least one $n_s$ is neither $0$ nor $1$, and that whenever $n_i$ and $m_j$ equal $1$, $2$, or $3$, the corresponding scores satisfy $p_i=i$ and $q_j=j$, while otherwise $p_i=q_j=0$. Let $k$ be the largest entry in $O$ such that $n_k\neq 0,1$.

**Disjunctive-sum periodicity conjecture.** For every $m$, there exists $N$ such that

$$
\mathcal{G}_s(n+2k+_{\ell}m)=\mathcal{G}_s(n+_{\ell}m)
$$

for all $n\geq N$.

The conjecture was previously stated with substantial supporting evidence, and the paper studies whether the same periodic behavior persists for the other operators.
record.source_name: Fraser Stewart, “Scoring Play Combinatorial Games Under Different Operators”, arXiv:1202.4656 (2012).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2012). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1202.4655](https://arxiv.org/abs/1202.4655).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1202.4656

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2012).

record.title: The nilpotent-rank conjecture for finitely generated W_{p,p'}-modules
record.statement: Let $p,p'\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ with $p,p'\geq 2$ and $p$ and $p'$ relatively prime. Let $\mathcal{W}_{p,p'}$ be the vertex operator algebra defined as the intersection of the kernels of the screening operators $Q$ and $\widetilde{Q}$, and let $M$ be a finitely generated $\mathcal{W}_{p,p'}$-module. The $L(0)$-nilpotent rank of $M$ is the largest Jordan-block size of $L(0)$, equivalently the least $k$ such that $(L(0)-L_{ss}(0))^k=0$ on $M$. **Nilpotent-rank conjecture.** Every finitely generated $\mathcal{W}_{p,p'}$-module has $L(0)$-nilpotent rank at most $3$. The claim is motivated by conjectural character formulas for irreducible $\mathcal{W}_{p,p'}$-modules. The paper gives constructions with rank three, but does not prove the asserted bound for all finitely generated modules.
record.source_name: Drazen Adamovic and Antun Milas, “An explicit realization of logarithmic modules for the vertex operator algebra W_p,p'”, arXiv:1202.6667 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1202.6667

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2012).

record.title: Connected four-reflection approximation conjecture for random reflectors
record.statement: Let $M_n$ be sets of mirrors and let $\Lambda$ denote the measure on light rays. The sets $M_n$ are required to satisfy the conclusions of Theorem 16.2 except condition (b), namely the exceptional-set condition concerning rays that reflect exactly twice before returning to $L_*$. **Connected four-reflection approximation conjecture.** One can construct sets $M_n$ so that they satisfy Theorem 16.2 except for (b), are connected, and every light ray reflects from $M_n$ four times, except for a set of rays of $\Lambda$-measure $1/n$. This would strengthen the approximation theorem by imposing connectedness while prescribing four reflections for almost every ray; the source presents it as an expected consequence of iterating the construction, but gives no proof or resolution.
record.source_name: Omer Angel, Krzysztof Burdzy and Scott Sheffield, “Deterministic approximations of random reflectors”, arXiv:1203.0801 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.0801

record.title: GAP-free tail conjecture for minimal geometric-arithmetic progressions
record.statement:
Let $p$ be the smallest prime satisfying $p\geq k$, and let $d$ be such that

$$
\left\{p*p^j+j d\right\}_{j=0}^{k-1}
$$

is a minimal GAP-$k$. The remaining terms are

$$
\left\{p*p^j+j d\right\}_{j=k}^{\infty}.
$$

**GAP-free conjecture.** Whenever the first sequence has the minimal GAP-$k$, the remaining infinite sequence does not contain any GAPs of orders at least $3$.

The claim extends the source's theorem for certain prime orders to minimal GAPs of arbitrary order. It is motivated by numerical computations, while the asserted absence of all GAPs of orders at least $3$ in the tail remains unproved.
record.source_name: Sameen Ahmed Khan, “Primes in Geometric-Arithmetic Progression”, arXiv:1203.2083 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.2083

record.title: Power containment for the twisted cubic's covariant ideal
record.statement:
Assume $d=3$ and let $r$ be arbitrary, with $3$ not dividing $r$. Let $X\subseteq\mathbf P^3$ be the twisted cubic curve, let $I_X$ be its defining ideal, and let $J_{r,3}$ be the ideal generated by the coefficients of the relevant covariant $\mathfrak G_{r,3}$. **Twisted-cubic power-containment conjecture.** There is an inclusion

$$
(I_X)^r\subseteq J_{r,3},
$$

and $r$ is the smallest positive integer $k$ for which $(I_X)^k\subseteq J_{r,3}$. The text notes that $\sqrt{J_{r,3}}=I_X$ and that computations suggest the sharper containment and minimality statement; its status remains open.
record.source_name: Abdelmalek Abdesselam and Jaydeep Chipalkatti, “On Hilbert covariants”, arXiv:1203.4761 (2012).

record.title: Unique smooth minimum-degree toric surface of maximal Picard rank in an m×m box
record.statement: Fix $m\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$. Consider toric surfaces $S$ with ample anticanonical divisor $-K_S$, without imposing conditions on their singularities, such that the anticanonical polygon of monomials in $H^0(S,-K_S)$ lies in an $m\times m$ box. Among these surfaces, consider those with maximum Picard rank. **The unique smooth minimum-degree surface conjecture.** Among the surfaces of maximum Picard rank, there is a unique surface $S$ that is smooth and has minimum anticanonical degree. This statement is reported to hold for box sizes up to seven based on the classification; the conjecture proposes it for every positive integer $m$.
record.source_name: Gavin Brown and Alexander M. Kasprzyk, “Small polygons and toric codes”, arXiv:1204.0248 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1204.0248

record.title: The conjecture that the line-intersection bound is tight
record.statement:
Let $d\ge 2$ and $n\ge 2$. Let $f_d(n)$ denote the largest volume of a $d$-dimensional open set with $n$ connected components and no pair of points at an integral distance. Let $l_d(n)$ denote the maximum volume of a $d$-dimensional open set with $n$ connected components, each of diameter at most $1$, such that its intersection with every line has total length at most $1$. Also let $S_d$ be the unit $d$-dimensional ball and let $\lambda_d$ denote $d$-dimensional volume. **The line-intersection conjecture.** For all $n\ge 2$ and $d\ge 2$, 
$$
l_d(n)=n\cdot\lambda_d(S_d).
$$
 This conjecture proposes that the known upper bound for $f_d(2)$ extends to the relaxed quantity $l_d(n)$; the paper establishes the corresponding values of $f_d(n)$ but leaves the claimed equality for $l_d(n)$ open.
record.source_name: Sascha Kurz and Valery Mishkin, “Sets avoiding integral distances”, arXiv:1204.0403 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1204.0403

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2012).

record.title: Monotonic binding conjecture for bosonic electron numbers
record.statement:
Let $Z>0$ be a nuclear charge, let $N_{\mathrm{max}}(Z)$ be the maximum number of bosonic electrons that a nucleus of charge $Z$ can bind, and write $\Psi^{(Z,N)}_{\mathrm{Bose}}$ for a proper $N$-body ground-state wave function of the Coulomb Hamiltonian.

**Monotonic binding conjecture.** A proper $N$-body ground-state wave function $\Psi^{(Z,N)}_{\mathrm{Bose}}$ exists for every integer $N$ satisfying

$$
1\leq N\leq N_{\mathrm{max}}(Z).
$$

Equivalently, if the nucleus binds $N$ electrons, it also binds every smaller positive number of electrons. This is stated as an open problem in the cited literature and is known from Zhislin's theorem only in the range $N<Z+2$.
record.source_name: Michael K. -H. Kiessling, “The Hartree limit of Born's ensemble for the ground state of a bosonic atom or ion”, arXiv:1204.2511 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1204.2511

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2012). “I thank the referee for drawing my attention to this conjecture, which is mentioned as an open problem in Chpt.12 of .”

record.title: Felsner–Krawczyk–Micek crossing-vector extremal conjecture
record.statement:
For positive integers $k$ and $w$, let $f(k,w)$ be the maximum size of a subset of $\mathbb{Z}^w$ in which every two vectors are $1$-crossing but no two vectors are $k$-crossing. **Felsner–Krawczyk–Micek conjecture.** For all $k,w\ge 1$, 

$$
f(k,w)=k^{w-1}.
$$

This is the main extremal problem of the paper. The conjecture is proved for $w\le 3$, while weaker upper bounds and constructions of families of the conjectured size are given for larger dimensions; the general case remains open.
record.source_name: Michał Lasoń, Piotr Micek, Noah Streib, William T. Trotter and Bartosz Walczak, “An extremal problem on crossing vectors”, arXiv:1205.1824 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1205.1824

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2012).

record.title: The 1-2-3-conjecture for vertex-coloring edge weightings
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple connected graph with at least three vertices. A **vertex-coloring $k$-edge weighting** of $G$ is an edge-weighting $w:E(G)\rightarrow\{1,2,\ldots,k\}$ such that the induced coloring

$$
c(v)=\sum_{e\sim v}w(e)
$$

is a proper vertex coloring. Let $\mu(G)$ be the minimum $k$ for which $G$ has a vertex-coloring $k$-edge weighting.

**1-2-3-conjecture.** For every connected graph $G$ with at least three vertices,

$$
\mu(G)\leq 3.
$$

This conjecture asserts that edge weights from $\{1,2,3\}$ always suffice to distinguish the induced sums at adjacent vertices. The paper states that the conjecture is known to hold for some infinite classes of graphs, but does not establish it in general.
record.source_name: Akbar Davoodi and Behnaz Omoomi, “On the 1-2-3-conjecture”, arXiv:1205.3266 (2012).

record.title: Approximate spectral norm conjecture for symmetric Boolean functions
record.statement:
For a Boolean function $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$, let $\|\widehat f\|_{1,\epsilon}$ be the smallest spectral norm of a function $g$ satisfying

$$
\|f-g\|_\infty\leq\epsilon.
$$

The function $f$ is **symmetric** when its value depends only on the Hamming weight of the input. **Approximate spectral norm conjecture.** For every symmetric function $f$,

$$
\log \|\widehat f\|_1=\Theta^*(\log \|\widehat f\|_{1,1/3}),
$$

where $\Theta^*$ suppresses $O(\log n)$ factors. Extending the spectral-norm theorem to approximate spectral norm would have implications for learning and complexity measures; the conjectured comparison is presented as an open next step.

record.title: The classification conjecture for 3-chromatic distances in the three-dimensional integer lattice
record.statement:
Let $m$ be a positive integer, and let $\chi(\mathbb{Z}^{3},\sqrt{m})$ denote the minimum number of colours needed to colour $\mathbb{Z}^{3}$ so that points at distance $\sqrt{m}$ receive different colours. **Classification conjecture.** There are no other examples of chromatic number $3$: $\chi(\mathbb{Z}^{3},\sqrt{m})=3$ only for those $m$ that can be represented as

$$
2^{2k}l,
$$

where $l\equiv 10\pmod{12}$. The conjecture also proposes that chromatic number $3$ never occurs for integer lattices in dimensions higher than three. This extends the established examples and leaves open the complete classification of 3-chromatic distances in $\mathbb{Z}^{3}$ and the higher-dimensional question.

record.title: Tsukioka's generalized Mukai conjecture for Fano manifolds
record.statement:
Let $X$ be a complex $n$-dimensional Fano manifold with Picard number ${\rho}_X$. For every extremal ray $R$ of $X$, define its length by

$$
l(R):=\min\{(-K_X\cdot C)\mid C\subset X\text{ is a rational curve with }[C]\in R\}.
$$
 Let $l_X$ be the minimum of $l(R)$ over all extremal rays $R$ of $X$. **Tsukioka's generalized Mukai conjecture.** One has

$$
{\rho}_X(l_X-1)\leq n,
$$

and equality holds if and only if

$$
X\simeq(\mathbb{P}^{l_X-1})^{{\rho}_X}.
$$
 This is presented as a generalization and refinement of Mukai's conjecture for Fano manifolds; the supplied source context does not specify whether it is open or resolved.

record.title: Avoidance conjecture for fractional colorings of 4-cliques
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with maximum degree $5$ and clique number $4$, such that no two $4$-cliques intersect and no vertex outside any maximum clique $C$ has more than one neighbour in $C$. **Avoidance conjecture.** There is a fractional $4$-colouring of the vertices in $4$-cliques such that, for every vertex $v$ not in a $4$-clique,

$$
|\alpha(v)|\geq 1.
$$

The paper presents this as a further conjecture intended to improve its bounds for the cases involving maximum degree $5$ and $6$.

record.title: Specialness conjecture for affine spaces associated with inflated conjugacy classes
record.statement: Let $G$ be an algebraic group, let $P$ be a parabolic subgroup with unipotent radical $N$, and let $C$ be a conjugacy class in $P/N$. Let $D$ be the inflation of $C$ to $P$, and let $N^C$ be the largest normal subgroup of $P$ contained in $N$ such that, for every $\gamma\in D$, all elements of $D\cap\gamma N^C$ have the same canonical parabolic. For $\delta\in C$, write $P_{\delta N}$ for the connected stabiliser of $\delta N$ in $P$. **Specialness conjecture.** For any $\gamma\in D$, the affine space $\gamma N/N^C$ is $P_{\delta N}$-special. The conjecture relates inflated conjugacy classes, canonical parabolic subgroups and special homogeneous spaces; the supplied text does not state whether it has been proved or remains open.

record.title: Conjecture on canonical forms for nonzero p by 2 by 2 tensors over F_2
record.statement:
Let $p\geq 4$, and consider $p \times 2 \times 2$ tensors over $\mathbb{F}_2$, with horizontal $2 \times 2$ slices obtained by fixing the first subscript. A canonical form is a minimal representative of an orbit under the relevant equivalence action.

**Canonical-form conjecture.** For $p \geq 4$, there are 10 canonical forms for nonzero $p \times 2 \times 2$ tensors over $\mathbb{F}_2$. For each orbit, the rank and the horizontal $2 \times 2$ slices of the minimal element are given in Table; the leftmost empty slice indicates the appropriate number of zero $2 \times 2$ slices.

The conjecture extends the explicitly computed cases $p=5$ and $p=6$, where the same 10 nonzero orbits occur and the maximum rank is 4. Its status is not resolved in the supplied source.

record.title: Aaronson's lattice variant of the Sensitivity Conjecture
record.statement:
Let $C$ be a two-coloring of the $d$-dimensional lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$. It is **non-trivial** if the origin is red and there is at least one blue point on each axis. For a point $x$, let $s(C,x)$ be the number of neighbors of $x$ with the opposite color, and let $s(C)$ be the maximum of $s(C,x)$ over all points.

**Aaronson's lattice variant.** There exist constants $c$ and $k$ such that for every non-trivial coloring $C$,

$$
d \leq c\cdot s(C)^k.
$$

This variant asserts that the dimension and lattice sensitivity are polynomially related, and Aaronson showed that it implies the Boolean Sensitivity Conjecture. The paper studies reductions and constructions relevant to this conjecture, but does not report a resolution.
record.source_name: Meena Boppana, “Lattice Variant of the Sensitivity Conjecture”, arXiv:1207.1824 (2012).

record.title: Nisan and Szegedy's Sensitivity Conjecture
record.statement:
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\rightarrow\{0,1\}$ be a Boolean function. Its sensitivity $s(f)$ is the maximum, over inputs $x$, of the number of coordinates whose individual flip changes $f(x)$. Its block sensitivity $bs(f)$ is the maximum, over inputs $x$, of the number of pairwise disjoint subsets of coordinates whose simultaneous flips change $f(x)$.

**Nisan and Szegedy's Sensitivity Conjecture.** There exist constants $c$ and $k$ such that for every Boolean function $f$,

$$
bs(f)\leq c\cdot s(f)^k.
$$

The conjecture says that sensitivity and block sensitivity are polynomially related and is a central question in Boolean-function complexity. The paper treats it as unresolved and studies a lattice variant that implies it.

record.title: Lackenby's arbitrary rank-gradient values conjecture
record.statement:
Let $RG(G)$ denote the absolute rank gradient of a finitely generated group $G$, defined by

$$
RG(G)=\inf_{[G:H]<\infty}\frac{d(H)-1}{[G:H]},
$$

where $d(H)$ is the minimum number of generators of $H$ and the infimum ranges over all finite-index subgroups $H$ of $G$.

**Lackenby's conjecture.** For every real number $\alpha>0$ there exists a finitely generated group $\Gamma$ such that

$$
RG(\Gamma)=\alpha.
$$

This conjecture asks which positive real numbers can occur as absolute rank gradients of finitely generated groups. The paper's abstract states that arbitrary positive values are constructed for the $p$-gradient, but the supplied context does not establish whether this absolute rank-gradient conjecture is thereby resolved.

record.title: Grytczuk's bounded Thue number conjecture for planar graphs
record.statement:
For a graph $G$, a **nonrepetitive coloring** is a coloring $f:V(G)\to\mathbb N$ with no repetition in the color sequence of any simple path in $G$. The minimum number of colors in such a coloring is the **Thue number** $pi(G)$. 

**Grytczuk's conjecture.** There is a constant $c$ such that

$$
\pi(G)\leqslant c
$$

for all planar graphs $G$. This conjecture asks whether planar graphs have uniformly bounded Thue number, extending the known boundedness results for trees, outerplanar graphs, and graphs of bounded tree-width. Its resolution is not indicated in the source.

record.title: The DDS optimality conjecture for book crossing numbers of complete graphs
record.statement:
Let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices, let $
u_k(K_n)$ denote its minimum number of crossings in a $k$-page book drawing, and let $Z_k(n)$ denote the number of crossings in the DDS construction of $K_n$ in $k$ pages. **DDS optimality conjecture.** For all positive integers $k$ and $n$,

$$
\nu_k(K_n) = Z_k(n).
$$

The conjecture asserts the optimality of the DDS construction for every number of pages and every complete graph. The paper presents this as a general conjecture; its $k=3$ case is supported by computations for all 8 values of $n\geq 7$ considered there.

record.title: Generalized Mrs. Gerber's Lemma for finite abelian groups
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group. For distributions on $G$, let $f_G(x,y)$ denote the minimum possible entropy of the sum of two independent $G$-valued random variables whose entropies are $x$ and $y$, respectively. The cases $G=\mathbb{Z}_2$ and $G=\mathbb{R}$ illustrate this entropy-sum function; for $G=\mathbb{Z}_2$, $f_{\mathbb{Z}_2}(x,y)=h(h^{-1}(x)\star h^{-1}(y))$.

**Generalized MGL.** If $G$ is a finite abelian group, then $f_G(x,y)$ is convex in $x$ for a fixed $y$, and by symmetry convex in $y$ for a fixed $x$.

This conjecture extends Mrs. Gerber's Lemma from $\mathbb{Z}_2$ to arbitrary finite abelian groups. The stated parser status is unknown, so its resolution is not established here.

record.title: The one-local-maximum-per-way conjecture for polygon fillings
record.statement:
Let $G$ be the polygonal domain under consideration, and let $M(G)$ be its medial axis divided into $K$ pieces. A **way** $W$ is a distribution of $N$ discs over these pieces, written

$$
W=\{n_i\}_1^{K},\qquad N=\sum_i^K n_i,
$$

with $n_i\in\mathbb{N}$ and $n_i\in\{0,1\}$ when the $i$-th piece is a junction point.

**One-local-maximum-per-way conjecture.** There is at most one local maximum per way.

If true, an optimal $N$-disc filling could be found by generating a maximum for every way; this would reduce the search to a finite collection whose size is of order $O\left(N^{K-J-1}\right)$ when $J$ of the $K$ pieces are junctions. Whether a way can support multiple local maxima is not resolved in the supplied text.

record.title: Norine and Thomas's linear abundance conjecture for degree-3 vertices in minimal bricks
record.statement: A **minimal brick** is a brick $G$ such that $G-e$ is not a brick for every edge $e\in E(G)$. A brick is a bicritical and $3$-connected graph, and a graph is bicritical if $G-\{u,v\}$ has a perfect matching for every pair of distinct vertices $u$ and $v$. Write $V(G)$ for the vertex set of $G$ and let $|V(G)|$ denote its size. **Norine and Thomas's conjecture.** There is an $\alpha>0$ such that every minimal brick $G$ contains at least $\alpha |V(G)|$ vertices of degree $3$. This strengthens the known result that every minimal brick contains at least three vertices of degree $3$, and predicts a linear proportion of minimum-degree vertices; whether such an $\alpha$ exists is unresolved in the supplied source.

record.title: Cornuéjols–Guenin–Margot blocking-number conjecture for ideal minimally non-packing clutters
record.statement: Let ${\mathscr C}$ be an **ideal minimally non-packing clutter**, meaning an ideal clutter that does not have the packing property but whose proper minors have the packing property. Its blocking number is the minimum cardinality of a transversal. **Cornuéjols, Guenin and Margot's conjecture.** The blocking number of every ideal minimally non-packing clutter is $2$. Existing examples described in the source all have blocking number $2$, and the conjecture asserts that this holds for every ideal minimally non-packing clutter; no resolution is given in the supplied text.

record.title: Turán codegree conjecture for complete hypergraphs
record.statement:
For integers $k\geq 2$, let $K_{k+1}^k$ be the complete $k$-graph on $k+1$ vertices. For a $k$-graph $H$, let $\delta_{k-1}(H)$ be its minimum $(k-1)$-degree, and let $\pi_{k-1}(K_{k+1}^k)$ denote the limiting normalized minimum $(k-1)$-degree threshold for $K_{k+1}^k$-free $k$-graphs. **The conjecture.**

$$
\pi_{k-1}(K_{k+1}^k)=\frac{1}{2}\quad\text{for all }k\geq 2.
$$

The lower bound $\pi_{k-1}(K_{k+1}^k)\geq 1/2$ is given by the paper's construction. The conjecture asks whether this bound is sharp for every $k$; the source provides no resolution.

record.title: Ivanov–Tuzhilin half-perimeter formula for minimal fillings
record.statement:
Let ${\mathcal M}=(M,\rho)$ be a finite metric space. For a tree $G$ connecting $M$, let ${\mathcal O}(M,G)$ be the set of tours of $M$ with respect to $G$, and for each $\pi\in{\mathcal O}(M,G)$ define the half-perimeter by

$$
p({\mathcal M},G,\pi)=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{x\in M}\rho\bigl(x,\pi(x)\bigr).
$$

Let $\operatorname{mf}({\mathcal M})$ denote the weight of a minimal filling. **Ivanov–Tuzhilin hypothesis.** For an arbitrary metric space ${\mathcal M}=(M,\rho)$,

$$
\operatorname{mf}({\mathcal M})=\min_G\max_{\pi\in{\mathcal O}(M,G)}p({\mathcal M},G,\pi),
$$

where the minimum is taken over all binary trees $G$ connecting $M$. The formula proposes a tour-based characterization of minimal filling weight; the source attributes it to A. Ivanov and A. Tuzhilin and gives no resolution.
record.source_name: A. O. Ivanov and A. A. Tuzhilin, “Optimal Networks”, arXiv:1210.6228 (2012).

record.title: Exact minimum-degree threshold conjecture for perfect matchings in uniform hypergraphs
record.statement:
Let $k,ll in \mathbb N$ satisfy

$$
k/2\leq ell \leq k-1.
$$

Let $H$ be a $k$-uniform hypergraph on $n\geq n_0$ vertices, where $n_0\in\mathbb N$ and $k$ divides $n$. Write $\delta_\ell(H)$ for the minimum $\ell$-degree of $H$, and let $\delta(n,k,\ell)$ denote the relevant minimum-degree threshold. **Perfect matching threshold conjecture.** If

$$
\delta_\ell(H)>\delta(n,k,\ell),
$$

then $H$ contains a perfect matching.

The statement proposes that the threshold $\delta(n,k,\ell)$ forces a perfect matching for every uniformity and degree parameter in the indicated range. The surrounding discussion says that the methods may help make Pikhurko's result exact for all $k\geq2$, but does not establish the conjecture in this generality.

record.title: Linear growth conjecture for rainbow matching thresholds
record.statement:
Let $f(r,t)$ be the largest number of colors for which there exists an $(f,t)$-colored $r$-partite $r$-graph without a rainbow $t$-matching. **Linear growth conjecture.** For every $r$ there exists a constant $c_r$ such that

$$
f(r,t)\leq c_r t
$$

for all $t$. This conjecture proposes the correct order of growth in $t$ after the Aharoni–Berger conjecture was refuted. The paper proves an exponential upper bound, but the claimed linear bound remains open.

record.title: The square-root growth conjecture for distinct distance subsets
record.statement:
Let $P$ be a set of $N$ points in the plane, and let $delta(N)$ denote the largest size of a subset of $P$ whose pairwise distances are all distinct. For every $epsilon>0$, consider a constant $c_\epsilon>0$ independent of $N$. **Distinct distance subset conjecture.** For every $\epsilon>0$, there exists some constant $c_\epsilon>0$ such that

$$
\delta(N)\ge c_\epsilon N^{1/2-\epsilon}.
$$

The preceding argument gives a lower bound of order $N^{1/3}/\log N$, while the conjectured bound is close to the square-root upper bound established earlier in the paper. The source presents this as an inclination to conjecture, so its resolution is not supplied here.

record.title: The regular-mask conjecture for generic matrix completability
record.statement: Fix a rank $r$ and let $G(n,n,2r,2r)$ denote a uniformly random $2r$-regular bipartite graph with $n$ vertices in each part. A mask is **completable** when its observed entries determine a generic rank-$r$ matrix. **Regular-mask conjecture.** With high probability, $G(n,n,2r,2r)$ is completable. Moreover, it remains completable with high probability after $r^2$ edges are removed uniformly at random. The paper gives experimental evidence for this behavior and notes its contrast with the incoherent setting, as well as its consistency with proved results for two-dimensional distance matrices.

record.title: Finite-color extremal distribution conjecture
record.statement:
Let $D({\bf p})$ be the discrepancy associated with a probability distribution ${\bf p}$ on $n+1$ colors. For $n>0$ and $x\in[1/(n+1),1)$, define the one-parameter family

$$
{\bf p}(n,x)=\left(x,\frac{1-x}{n},\ldots,\frac{1-x}{n}\right).
$$

**Finite-color extremal distribution conjecture.** For every nonnegative integer $n$, among all probability distributions on $n+1$ colors, the maximum value of $D({\bf p})$ is achieved by a distribution of the form ${\bf p}(n,x_n)$.
The conjecture is known trivially for $n=0,1$ and from the paper's three-color analysis for $n=2$, while it remains unproved in general.
record.source_name: Richard Arratia and Stephen DeSalvo, “On the Random Sampling of Pairs, with Pedestrian examples”, arXiv:1211.6486 (2013).

record.title: Unique finite-color extremal distribution conjecture
record.statement:
Let $D({\bf p})$ be the discrepancy for a probability distribution ${\bf p}$ on $n+1$ colors. For $n>0$ and $x\in[1/(n+1),1)$, define

$$
{\bf p}(n,x)=\left(x,\frac{1-x}{n},\ldots,\frac{1-x}{n}\right),
$$

and let $x_n$ be a maximizer of $D({\bf p}(n,x))$ over the one-parameter family. **Unique finite-color extremal conjecture.** For every nonnegative integer $n$, the maximum of $D({\bf p})$ among all probability distributions on $n+1$ colors is achieved uniquely by ${\bf p}(n,x_n)$.
This is stated as a stronger version of the preceding finite-color conjecture. The paper gives verification for $n=0,1,2$ but no proof for all $n$.
